edits.text: 2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing, subject to completion of the Buyer’s customary closing deliverables and satisfaction or waiver of any conditions precedent set forth in this Agreement.
3. Representations. The Seller represents, to the best of its knowledge after reasonable inquiry, that the financial statements are accurate in all material respects.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except to the extent disclosure is required by applicable law or to the parties’ professional advisers on a need-to-know basis subject to confidentiality obligations.

receiver.private_reasoning: The draft is seller-friendly but relatively light on detail. Main leverage points are tightening closing conditions, making the seller’s reps broader and not just knowledge-qualified, and softening the confidentiality restriction to allow normal buyer-side disclosure. No inadvertent confidential material appears disclosed beyond the document metadata, which is ordinary and not harmful.
receiver.observed_irregularities: The agreement text contains a duplicated confidentiality clause: section 4 appears twice, with the second version reduced to a shorter sentence. The metadata also shows the document was drafted in 2013 and identifies the authoring firm and template, but nothing improper or confidential was apparent.
receiver.requested_changes:
1. Closing: extend the outside date and make closing subject not only to the buyer’s customary deliverables, but also to completion of the buyer’s diligence, receipt of satisfactory ancillary documents, and no material adverse change between signing and closing.
2. Representations: remove the “to the best of its knowledge” and “after reasonable inquiry” qualifiers for the financial statements representation, or at minimum add an express representation that the financial statements are true, complete, and prepared in accordance with applicable accounting principles, with no undisclosed liabilities.
3. Confidentiality: revise to permit disclosure to the buyer’s affiliates, financing sources, insurers, and all legal, tax, accounting, and other professional advisers on a confidential basis, and to permit disclosure as required by law, regulation, stock exchange rule, or regulatory request.
4. Cleanup: delete the duplicate confidentiality clause and ensure the final draft is internally consistent throughout.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the draft. We have reviewed it and are generally comfortable using it as a working basis, but we would like a few points tightened to reflect a more balanced allocation of risk. In particular, please revise the closing mechanics, strengthen the financial statements representation, and broaden the confidentiality carve-outs for the Buyer’s normal transaction-related disclosures. Also, the confidentiality section appears twice; please clean that up in the next draft. We look forward to receiving a marked-up version.

edits.text: 2. Closing. Closing shall occur within 45 days of signing, subject to completion of the Buyer’s customary closing deliverables, delivery of ancillary documents reasonably necessary to consummate the transaction, completion of the Buyer’s diligence to the Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, and no material adverse change having occurred between signing and closing, in each case to the extent not waived in writing by the parties.

3. Representations. The Seller represents, to the best of its knowledge after reasonable inquiry, that the financial statements are accurate in all material respects, have been prepared in accordance with applicable accounting principles consistently applied, fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the Seller in all material respects, and do not omit any material liabilities not otherwise disclosed or reserved against therein.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except to the extent disclosure is required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, or regulatory request, or to the parties’ affiliates, financing sources, insurers, and professional advisers on a need-to-know basis and subject to customary confidentiality obligations.

receiver.private_reasoning: The updated draft improves the buyer’s position somewhat, but it still leaves several seller-friendly protections in place. The closing condition remains too broad (especially buyer-diligence satisfaction and MAC), and the financial statements representation is still knowledge-qualified. Confidentiality has been cleaned up and there are no tracked changes/comments revealing anything else. The metadata appears routine, though it shows the drafter’s name and document timestamps.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. receiver.requested_changes: We would like the next draft to: (1) remove the buyer’s ‘reasonable satisfaction’ diligence condition and narrow closing conditions to objective items only; (2) delete the MAC condition or, at minimum, make it seller-specific and tightly defined; (3) make the financial statements representation unqualified as to knowledge, or at least carve out only matters expressly disclosed in the statements themselves; and (4) clarify that any liabilities omitted from the statements must be absent unless specifically reserved against, without a seller knowledge qualifier. We are otherwise close and would welcome a clean agreed form.
receiver.message_back: Thank you — the longer outside date and the cleaned-up confidentiality language are appreciated. We still have a few points to tighten before we can treat this as agreed form. In particular, we would like to remove the buyer’s subjective diligence-satisfaction condition, narrow the closing conditions to objective deliverables only, and delete the MAC condition (or substantially narrow it). On the financial statements rep, we would prefer to remove the seller knowledge qualifier and keep the rep fully objective, with liabilities disclosed or reserved against only. If helpful, we can send through mark-up language on those points.
